== Biography ==
Thomas was born before 1700.

Thomas Glasgow, born before 1700 and Cathrine Clarkson has 7 children between 1717-1735.

* Margaret Glasgow May 12 1717 in Uphall, Linlithgowshire, Scotland<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4Z-NYQ : 11 February 2020), Thomas Glasgow in entry for Margaret Glasgow, 1717.</ref>
* Abraham Mar 29 1719<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ48-MZH : 11 February 2020), Thomas Glasgow in entry for Abraham Glasgow, 1719.https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ48-MZH</ref>
* Alexander Feb 7 1721<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ48-994 : 11 February 2020), Thomas Glasgow in entry for Alexander Glasgow, 1721.</ref> in Uphall, Linlithgowshire, Scotland
* James Apr 7 1723 in Uphall, Linlithgowshire<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4Z-Y5S : 11 February 2020), Thomas Glasgow in entry for James Glasgow, 1723.</ref>
* Andrew Jan 1730in Livingston, Linlithgowshire <ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1RG-YV2 : 11 February 2020), Thomas Glasgow in entry for Andrew Glasgow, 1730.</ref>
* Mary 23 Jan 1732 in Livingston, Linlithgowshire, Scotland<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1R2-5XY : 11 February 2020), Thomas Glasgou in entry for Mary Glasgou, 1732.</ref>
* Hellen 18 Oct 1735 in Livingston, Linlithgowshire  <ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1R2-KB6 : 11 February 2020), Thomas Glasgou in entry for Hellen Glasgou, 1735</ref>

Alt spellings, Catharin Classon, Katrin Classon, Cathrine Clerkson.


== Research Notes ==
=== Uphall household review, 23 October 2026 ===

Assess John Glasgow-1105 as Thomas Glasgow-1226’s possible father at 30%, previously 22%. The 1701 Thomas/Jean marriage is now anchored in Linlithgow, and the 1716 banns place the Clarkson groom specifically at Uphall before the 1717–1735 child sequence. Together with the Duncan household’s 1704 and 1711 Uphall entries, this makes a local succession more specific than a repeated surname alone. The proposed 1675 Linlithgow child would be about 26 at the 1701 marriage, 41 at the Clarkson banns and 60 at the last 1735 child. This is a coherent, if increasingly late, fatherhood sequence. The modest increase recognises the dated local fit; it does not assert remarriage or a proved identity. 30% is a subjective assessment of the complete Clarkson-adult → John-1105 proposition. Two identity bridges remain unproved: the 1675 child to the Duncan groom, and the Duncan father to the Clarkson groom. No widowhood, remarital status, age, trade or parent is given in the inspected marriage transcripts. Jean’s death is not established. An unrecorded younger local Thomas remains a serious alternative; Thomas-1311 (1666) and Thomas-3091 (1663) are older compatible rivals. The 1679 Carstairs/Spence groom is not an established identity for this adult. The unverified 1766 memorial contributes no weight. The 1715 Edinburgh citation is excluded from the supporting sequence. Both Thomas accounts remain separate and no biological or profile merge is made.

The newly inspected Findmypast transcripts establish Thomas Glasgow and Jean Duncan’s Linlithgow banns on 30 March 1701 (groom a servant; witnesses James Craw and William Duncan) and marriage on 4 May 1701. The banns leave both residences as question marks. A third Linlithgow register index names the same couple in 1701 without a day. These are related register entries, not three independent family identifications.

Kirkliston banns dated 22 June 1716 name Thomas Glasgon, resident at Uphall, and Catharine Clerkson, resident at Kirkliston. The named couple, Uphall residence and Margaret’s following 1717 Uphall child entry identify the existing Clarkson household. The FamilySearch-derived duplicate calls this a marriage date; retain the more specific banns label from OPR 667/1, item 5, rather than asserting a ceremony on that day.

Two Findmypast FamilySearch-derived entries name Philip Glasgow, male, baptised 3 June 1711 at Uphall, father Thomas Glasgow and mother Jean Duncan. They corroborate the maintained Scottish child account and do not identify a Mary. The older Mary label is an editorial inconsistency, not a second contemporary child. The separate family citation giving 21 October 1711/Linlithgow remains an unresolved index discrepancy: its underlying page was inaccessible and the present search did not find it. Duplicate transcriptions do not supply independent testimony.

The 15 June 1715 Edinburgh child is already represented by Thomas Glasgow-1243, whose selected father is the Edinburgh baxter Thomas Glasgow-3285. His transcript explicitly calls the father a baxter and indweller. This citation must not be used as another Uphall/Duncan birth or evidence for the proposed Duncan-to-Clarkson succession. The recorded Edinburgh father is retained as a separately identified household; no record establishes its identity with the Uphall father.

30% is a subjective assessment of the complete Clarkson-adult → John-1105 proposition. Two identity bridges remain unproved: the 1675 child to the Duncan groom, and the Duncan father to the Clarkson groom. No widowhood, remarital status, age, trade or parent is given in the inspected marriage transcripts. Jean’s death is not established. An unrecorded younger local Thomas remains a serious alternative; Thomas-1311 (1666) and Thomas-3091 (1663) are older compatible rivals. The 1679 Carstairs/Spence groom is not an established identity for this adult. The unverified 1766 memorial contributes no weight. The 1715 Edinburgh citation is excluded from the supporting sequence. Both Thomas accounts remain separate and no biological or profile merge is made.

Inspect the original 1701 and 1716 entries for fuller residence, occupation and marital status; seek Jean Duncan’s burial or a property/probate passage connecting the two households. Reconcile the separate 21 October 1711 citation. An explicit age or family network could distinguish the 1675 child from younger local Thomas namesakes.

The dated review above supersedes earlier statements that the 1701 marriage was only family information, that the 1711 child was Mary, or that the 1715 Edinburgh child supports the Uphall sequence. Other earlier evidence and unresolved alternatives remain below.

=== Selected uncertain family — 16 October 2026 ===

Select John [[Glasgow-1105]] and Agnes Eastone-3 as the uncertain working parents of Thomas [[Glasgow-1226]], the father with Catherine Clarkson/Classon at Uphall from 1717 and Livingston by 1730. This selects possible identity with their named Linlithgow child Thomas [[Glasgow-1242]] of 1675, while retaining both profile accounts. That child would be about 42 at the 1717 Margaret entry and about 60 at the 1735 Hellen entry: later fatherhood, but chronologically possible. The existing Glasgow-1242 account also represents a Thomas/Jean Duncan household at Uphall in 1704. Recurring Thomas name, the same Uphall parish and a plausible succession of households provide a more specific route than the removed Kilbirnie-minister parents. The 1675 parent clause belongs directly to the child account; transferring it to the Clarkson adult depends wholly on the uncertain identity.

Agnes’s maternity is assessed separately: the 1675 FamilySearch parent index explicitly identifies Agnes Eastone in Thomas Glesgow’s entry, while John is named as father in the paired child citation. This is a positive maternal source for that child, not merely John’s spouse field. Agnes’s attachment to the Clarkson adult remains uncertain because the child/adult identity is uncertain. Eastone/Daston readings, her estimated birth and John’s own child/adult identification remain qualified. These two new parent links share one identity premise and are correlated, not independent confirmations of the adult’s ancestry.

The 1675 child, the Duncan adult and the Clarkson adult may represent one, two or three men. There is no inspected age, occupation, marriage, widowhood or probate bridge. The 1701 Duncan marriage is reported family information, not a newly inspected register. No death of Jean, remarriage to Catherine or overlap resolution is invented. The differing Philip 1711 dates in the Thomas research compilation and the Glasgow-1242 biography, and the omission of a mother in the latter’s indexed child, do not establish a continuous Duncan household or certain maternity. They are not two independent confirmations. Catherine’s indexed surname variants remain as recorded. The before 1700 boundary for the Clarkson adult and the 2/21 February 1675 date discrepancy in the child account remain unchanged. The 1666 St Cuthbert’s Thomas-1311, child of Alexander and Issobell Anderson, remains a compatible identity alternative, albeit with fatherhood at about 51–69 in 1717–1735. His possible identification with the Edinburgh writer whose testament was indexed in 1691 is unproved and cannot be used to exclude him. The retained 1766 grave link is an unverified namesake comparison, not an established death for the Clarkson adult. The 1663 Thomas-3091 and an otherwise unrecorded local Thomas also remain possible. No identity merge or live attachment is performed.
